The instant petition was filed on 17.01.2023 and listed for hearing on 16.05.2023, wherein the Commission, after hearing the submissions of the parties, admitted the petition. Based on the request of the parties, the Commission permitted the parties to file their respective written submissions. Pursuant to the directions of this Commission, SECI filed its Reply on 02.09.2023, while BRPL filed its reply on 30.11.2023. Subsequently, hearings were held on 28.11.2023 and 12.02.2024. During the hearing held on 12.02.2024, BRPL & BYPL sought an adjournment since the arguing counsel was not present, and BYPL also sought an adjournment for filing the reply. The Commission took a strong exception to such a casual approach of BYPL and allowed the prayer to upload its reply within a week at a cost of Rupees Ten Thousand. Subsequently, BYPL filed its response on 16.02.2024. During the hearing held on 08.07.2025, the parties made detailed submissions, and thereafter, the matter was reserved for order subject to the filing of written submissions (if any). - i) The Petitioner is required to establish a one to one correlation between the project, the supply of goods against which change in law is claimed, the invoices and other relevant documents for proof of the payment of claimed amount on account of change in law. - n) The aspect of the methodology for payment of amount on account of Change in law need to be considered based on the decision of this Commission in regard to admissibility of the events claimed by the Petitioner as Change in Law within the scope of Article 12 of the PPA. - p) The Commission may be pleased to take into consideration the above aspects in regard to the payment mechanism for the impact of alleged Change in Law events if held to be admissible to the Petitioner. - q) If the events claimed by the Petitioner are considered as Change in Law and the impact is allowed to the Petitioner, the Commission may be pleased to issue directions to BRPL and BYPL (i.e. the procurers of power under the respective PSAs), to make payment towards the evaluated change in law claims payable by SECI to Petitioner, on a back to back basis as per Article 8.2.3 of the respective PSAs. - u) It is settled principle that in the matters of restitution, the courts should adopt pragmatic view and grant relief in a manner as may be reasonable, fair and practicable. The contentions of BRPL in this regard are wrong and denied and have been addressed in the subsequent paragraphs. - f) The Petitioner had provided bona fide estimates of the monetary impact of the Change in Law event and had further craved leave to furnish details of actual expenditure at the time of reconciliation. The Commission in similar matters has consistently directed parties to carry out a reconciliation process to verify the actual expenditure incurred along with Carrying Cost by exhibiting clear one-to-one correlation between the Project and the invoices for supply of goods and services on which the Change in Law compensation is claimed. - g) The Petitioner has always been ready and willing to reconcile its Change in Law claims with SECI by providing all relevant documents including date of delivery of goods, invoices, date on which invoices were raised, etc. 16.
